newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul shares at fourth record close in a row.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul shares at fourth record close in a row.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted selective gains on Friday, with the market index hitting its fourth consequtive high in the continuing uptrend.

The IMKB National-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,194, up 14 points, or 1.19 percent from Thursday's previous record of 1,180. In dollar terms, it rose slightly to 1.06 cents from yesterday's record of 1.05 cents.
Trade volume fell to 22.96 trillion lira ($203.5 million) from Thursday's 26.30 trillion ($234.3 million).
Brokers said afternoon profit-taking prompted by expectations of resistance at the 1,200 level caused the index to retreit from a midday record of 1,198.

Brokers said the market would await a constitutional court ruling next week on a law designed to enable the privatisation of Turk Telekom, the centrepiece of the government's ambitious 1997 sell-off programme aimed at reducing huge deficits.
"Next week, fears of a cancellation in the Telekom law and difficulty to overcome the 1,200 resistance after another test may lead to a down correction towards 1,170," Ozcan said.
The index has surged 22.34 percent, breaking 11 record closes since January 2 when the market reopened after a five-day holiday.
